newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-TENDULKAR CENTURY GIVES ADVANTAGE TO INDIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TENDULKAR CENTURY GIVES ADVANTAGE TO INDIA.

text.p: Sachin Tendulkar hit his 12th test century to help ease India into a commanding position at lunch on the second day of the first test against Sri Lanka on Sunday.
The Indian skipper was unbeaten on 112 as India went to lunch at 386 for three. Former captain Mohammad Azharuddin, who has ably supported Tendulkar, was not out on 73.
When India resumed at 280 for three in the morning interest mostly centred around Tendulkar's hundred, his third against Sri Lanka.
He needed 44 minutes to add the remaining runs to his overnight score of 65. His century included 18 fours and took 162 minutes and 143 balls to complete.
Azharuddin playing an equally prominent role, completing his 17th test half-century, which included seven fours, in 101 minutes off 65 balls.
The two bought up their century partnership in 89 minutes and by lunch they had added 156 runs to the Indian score.
Sri Lanka's Ravindra Pushpakumar came in for heavy punishment from Azharuddin who plundered four fours in one of his overs, leaving the bowler with figures of one for 96 off 19 overs at lunch.
On a slow and placid track Sri Lankan bowlers toiled hard for success without much luck as both Tendulkar and Azharuddin batted throughout the session adding 106 runs off 30 overs.
